An extra state payment could help cover a utility bill, replenish savings, keep more cash in your wallet , or give your budget some breathing room. Depending on where you live, receiving that money might not require a separate application. New York offers automatic energy rebate checks, and Georgia issues surplus tax refunds using eligible taxpayers' records. New Jersey automatically files property tax relief applications for many returning participants. Oregon takes a different approach, returning surplus revenue through a credit claimed on a tax return. Virginia's earlier rebate also deserves a look if you qualified but never received your payment. The important questions are which program applies to you, whether you met its filing requirements, and whether the money is still coming or was already included in an earlier refund. Read More Here › SPONSORED New York New York's Protecting Our Wallets Energy Rebate, or POWER, program provides one-time checks of up to $200 to qualifying taxpayers. Mailings began September 21, 2026, with deliveries scheduled to continue through December. Eligibility requires full-year New York residency in 2024, a timely 2024 resident income tax return, income within the program's limits, and not being claimed as someone else's dependent. Joint filers and qualifying surviving spouses receive $200 with 2024 New York adjusted gross income of $150,000 or less. Those with income above $150,000 through $300,000 receive $150. Single filers, heads of household, and married taxpayers filing separately receive $100 with income of $150,000 or less. Eligible taxpayers don't need to apply. Payments arrive by paper check, even if their regular tax refund was directly deposited. The state mails checks to the most current address it has on file. If you moved, confirm your address through your New York Individual Online Services account. Shopping for cheaper auto insurance? Enter your zip code here to get started. Georgia Georgia's automatic surplus tax refund of up to $500 returns some or all of an eligible taxpayer's 2024 state income taxes, subject to limits based on filing status. Single taxpayers and married people filing separately can receive up to $250. Heads of household can receive up to $375, while married couples filing jointly can receive up to $500. Qualifying taxpayers must have timely filed both their 2024 and 2025 Georgia income tax returns and have qualifying 2024 tax liability. For taxpayers with a valid extension, the 2025 return deadline was October 15, 2026. The maximum payment isn't guaranteed. A smaller 2024 tax liability can mean a smaller refund, and qualifying part-year residents and nonresidents receive prorated amounts. Certain state debts can also reduce the payment. For eligible taxpayers who already filed, no separate claim is generally required. Taxpayers who used an ITIN may need to respond to a Department of Revenue letter requesting additional information to determine eligibility. If you expected a payment, check Georgia's official surplus refund status tool before assuming another application is necessary. New Jersey New Jersey's ANCHOR program offers property tax relief to qualifying homeowners and renters. The 2026 payment cycle uses 2025 eligibility information. Applicants must have owned or rented and lived in their principal New Jersey residence on October 1, 2025, and met the applicable property and income requirements. Eligible homeowners generally receive $1,500 with income of $150,000 or less, or $1,000 with income from $150,001 through $250,000. Eligible renters with income of $150,000 or less generally receive $450 if they were 64 or younger in 2025, or $700 if they were 65 or older. Many returning participants have applications filed automatically using their prior-year application information. This includes qualifying homeowners under 65 who don't receive Social Security or Railroad Retirement disability benefits, and qualifying renters of all ages. Automatic filing doesn't cover everyone. Senior homeowners and homeowners receiving those disability benefits generally must complete the combined PAS-1 application. The application deadline was November 2, 2026. Check your confirmation letter and benefit status rather than assuming that filing an income tax return alone enrolled you. Payments began in September, with automatically filed applicants beginning to receive benefits in October. Payments are distributed on a rolling basis. Learn More Here › SPONSORED Oregon Oregon's "kicker" returns excess state revenue through a credit on the 2025 income tax return filed in 2026. The credit equals 9.863% of a taxpayer's qualifying 2024 Oregon tax liability. For example, a qualifying liability of $3,000 produces a $295.89 credit. To qualify, taxpayers must file a 2024 Oregon return, have Oregon tax liability for that year, and file a 2025 Oregon return, even if they wouldn't otherwise need to file. The kicker generally doesn't arrive as a separate automatic check. Instead, claiming it can increase your state refund or reduce the amount you owe. If you already filed your 2025 return, review it to see whether the credit was included before counting on additional money. Oregon also provides a "What's My Kicker?" calculator to help taxpayers determine their amount. Virginia Virginia's 2025 rebate provided up to $200 for individual filers and up to $400 for married couples filing jointly. Eligibility required 2024 state income tax liability and filing the qualifying return by November 3, 2025. The rebate was limited by the taxpayer's liability after applicable deductions, subtractions, and credits. This is an earlier payment program. Virginia's current rebate page describes eligible taxpayers as having received their payments, so it shouldn't be treated as a newly announced 2026 check. However, the state tells eligible taxpayers who never received their rebate to contact Virginia Tax. Reviewing your return and payment records could help you determine whether you need to follow up. Bottom line State relief can arrive as an automatic check, a direct deposit, a property tax benefit, or a credit on your return. Your next step depends on the program's rules and whether you already received the benefit. Start with your state's official program page, then compare the required tax years and deadlines with your records. Confirm whether you needed to claim the benefit and whether it was included in an earlier refund. If you qualified for a payment that never arrived, use the state's published status or contact options. A quick review could help you find money you missed and better prepare yourself financially for upcoming expenses.
